refsect1.title: Introduction
refsect1.para: systemd-timesyncd.service8 is a system service that may be used to synchronize the local system clock with a remote Network Time Protocol (NTP) server. This page describes the D-Bus interface.

refsect1.title: The Manager Object
refsect1.para: The service exposes the following interfaces on the Manager object on the bus:

PHC indicates whether PTP hardware clocks tagged timesync in udev are used, if available, as configured with PHC= in timesyncd.conf5. PHCDeviceMatch contains the device node path configured there, if any, in which case the device with this device node path or symlink is used instead, regardless of its tags. PHCDevice contains the device node of the PTP hardware clock the system clock is currently synchronized to, and PHCClockName its name as reported by the kernel driver. Both are empty if no PTP hardware clock is in use (in which case NTP is used). PHCOffsetNSec and PHCDelayNSec contain the offset of the PTP hardware clock relative to the system clock and the read delay, as determined by the most recent measurement, in nanoseconds. PHCSampleCount and PHCJitterUSec contain the number of samples taken from the PTP hardware clock so far, and their jitter. While a PTP hardware clock is in use, NTPMessage reports an empty message with a packet count of zero.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: The org.freedesktop.timesync1 D-Bus API was added in version 239.

refsect2.title: The Manager Object
refsect2.para: PHC, PHCDeviceMatch, PHCDevice, PHCClockName, PHCOffsetNSec, PHCDelayNSec, PHCSampleCount, and PHCJitterUSec were added in version 263.
